questions.q: What distinguishes a recoverable loss spike from divergence?
options: Recoverable spikes happen only during warmup; divergence happens only after warmup
A recoverable spike's loss returns to its prior trend within some steps, while divergence is a spike that does not self-correct and keeps drifting or oscillating
There is no meaningful difference between the two
Divergence only happens when using bf16
questions.explain: A spike that recovers on its own over subsequent steps is a routine blip; one that doesn't recover and keeps drifting or oscillating is divergence, which requires intervention.

questions.q: Why does bf16 cause fewer overflow-driven loss spikes than fp16?
options: bf16 uses more total bits than fp16
bf16 keeps fp32's wide exponent range (trading mantissa precision instead), so values are far less likely to overflow to inf than in fp16's narrow exponent range
bf16 is only used for inference, never training
bf16 automatically applies gradient clipping
questions.explain: bf16 and fp32 share the same 8-bit exponent range; bf16 reduces mantissa bits instead, which avoids the narrow dynamic range that makes fp16 prone to overflow.

questions.q: What does gradient clipping by global norm do?
options: It deletes any batch containing a large gradient
It computes the L2 norm across all parameter gradients and rescales every gradient proportionally if that norm exceeds a threshold
It increases the learning rate when gradients are small
It converts gradients from fp16 to bf16
questions.explain: Global-norm clipping measures the combined L2 norm of all gradients and, if it exceeds max_norm, scales every gradient down by the same factor so no single step moves the model too far.

questions.q: A team notices a sharp loss spike clustered right where the learning-rate schedule's warmup phase ends and the rate hits its peak. What does this pattern most directly suggest?
options: The tokenizer vocabulary is too small
The peak learning rate may be too aggressive for the model at this stage of training
The dataset has too few tokens
The GPU driver needs to be reinstalled
questions.explain: Spikes clustered right as the learning rate reaches its peak point to the peak rate itself being too high for the model's current training dynamics.

questions.q: What is the standard recovery procedure when monitoring shows a loss spike is not self-recovering (true divergence)?
options: Continue training unchanged and hope it stabilizes
Roll back to the last good checkpoint and resume, often skipping the offending data shard or lowering the learning rate slightly
Immediately restart the entire run from step zero
Switch the model to fp32 permanently for the rest of training
questions.explain: The standard response to true divergence is to restore the last good checkpoint and resume, typically adjusting for the suspected cause (skipping a bad shard, trimming LR) before continuing.
